overview: This Senate resolution marks the 10th anniversary of the Columbine Day of Service and honors the victims and survivors of the April 20, 1999, shooting at Columbine High School in Littleton, Colorado, where 12 students and a teacher were killed and 24 others were injured. The Day of Service was created to channel the community's response to the tragedy into volunteer work, and it has grown to include projects in several states and countries. The resolution offers condolences, recognizes community service as a way to rebuild after tragedy, and encourages Americans to remember the victims and take part in the annual Day of Service. It does not change any law or spending. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on May 14, 2026.
for: Supporters say the resolution honors the victims and survivors and highlights a community's effort to answer tragedy with service.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or policy related to school safety or violence prevention.
